summary: Ubisoft's Tom Clancy stealth-action series following Sam Fisher, with major version splits across PC, Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, PSP, mobile, and HD collection releases.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
entries.definitive_edition: Windows version with PS2-exclusive-level secondary plan

emulation.emulator: None for primary; PCSX2 and handheld/mobile emulators for secondary preservation
emulation.notes: Use native Windows for the main run; use PCSX2 only for the PS2-exclusive level.

primary.version: PC version based on the Xbox release with bonus missions
primary.why: Windows is closely based on the technically strongest Xbox version and includes the downloadable bonus missions, giving it the best fidelity-plus-content balance for the core game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with modern compatibility fixes applied; then use the PS2 route only for its exclusive Kola Cell/nuclear power plant level if full content coverage matters.

secondary.exclusive_content: Exclusive Kola Peninsula nuclear power plant level and added cinematics/interview material.
secondary.what_to_play: Play only the PS2-exclusive level and archive the PS2-exclusive video extras.
secondary.why: The PS2/GameCube builds are lower-fidelity and easier, but the PS2 version adds a unique story level absent from Windows/Xbox.

secondary.what_to_play: Preserve as a handheld/mobile adaptation rather than replaying the main campaign.
secondary.why: These are side-scrolling adaptations rather than straight ports.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PS3 HD Trilogy is not fully definitive for this entry because it lacks the downloadable bonus missions noted for the Xbox/PC route.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow
entries.definitive_edition: Windows current release with PS2/GameCube extra-mission secondary plan

emulation.emulator: None for primary; PCSX2/Dolphin and handheld/mobile emulators for secondary preservation
emulation.notes: Use native Windows for the main run; use PS2/GameCube emulation only for the additional mission.

primary.version: Current PC release with modern fixes
primary.why: Windows gives the highest-fidelity route, and Pandora Tomorrow has returned to PC storefronts with shadow-rendering issues addressed, while community fixes cover modern-resolution play.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release with modern/Fusion-style fixes; then use PS2 or GameCube only for the additional single-player mission.

secondary.exclusive_content: Additional single-player mission that compensates for abridged PS2/GameCube level design.
secondary.what_to_play: Play only the extra PS2/GameCube mission after finishing the Windows route.
secondary.why: The PS2/GameCube versions include an extra single-player mission.
The GBA/mobile releases are side-scrolling adaptations.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PC rerelease is still not a full remaster; document Ubisoft Connect/storefront requirements and applied fixes.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory

emulation.notes: Use native Windows; emulate console/handheld versions only for preservation comparison.

primary.why: The PC version is based on the strong Xbox build and adds PC rendering/resolution flexibility; it is the best main-campaign fidelity route when patched for modern systems.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with compatibility, widescreen, and controller fixes; archive portable versions separately only as downgraded adaptations.

entries.remaster_caveats: PS3 HD Trilogy and 3DS versions are convenience/portable routes, not the definitive fidelity route.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Essentials

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for upscaling and controller mapping; preserve original PSP behavior if comparing performance.

primary.why: Essentials was released only for PSP, so PPSSPP or original PSP hardware is the only route for its unique interstitial story and missions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release on PPSSPP with documented settings, or on original PSP hardware for strict preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; controls/performance are rough, so document PPSSPP control settings.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Double Agent
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox 360 HD version plus Xbox version-2 secondary playthrough

emulation.emulator: None for primary; Xemu/PCSX2/Dolphin optional for version-2 preservation
emulation.notes: Use Xbox backward compatibility for the HD run; use original Xbox hardware or Xemu for the version-2 campaign.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox 360 backward compatibility for HD version; Xbox/Xemu for version 2

primary.why: Double Agent has two materially different main versions. The Xbox 360/PS3/Windows version is the higher-fidelity HD version, but the PC port has major unresolved technical issues, making Xbox 360 via modern Xbox backward compatibility the best primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 version through Xbox backward compatibility where possible; then play the original Xbox version 2 separately for its different levels and storyline.

secondary.exclusive_content: Ubisoft Montreal version 2 with different storylines, plot twists, level designs, and order.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the original Xbox version 2 campaign after the HD version, or at least its different missions.
secondary.why: Two separate versions exist with different storylines, plot twists, and levels; the Xbox version is the best route for version 2.

secondary.what_to_play: Preserve as a mobile adaptation only.
secondary.why: A separate mobile-phone version was developed by Gameloft.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate the HD and sixth-gen versions; the PC port is not primary because of unresolved technical issues.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction

emulation.notes: Native Windows route; Xbox backward compatibility is useful for console comparison.

primary.version: PC release with Insurgency Pack/Deniable Ops content
primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the main campaign, co-op prologue, Deniable Ops, and DLC content; mobile/cloud releases are separate or historical routes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with compatibility fixes and the DLC installed; document server/co-op availability and any Ubisoft Connect requirements.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; document online/co-op state before archival capture.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Blacklist - Spider-Bot

emulation.notes: Use original mobile hardware or emulator only after documenting app version.

primary.why: Spider-Bot is a separate 2D puzzle tie-in released for Android and iOS before Blacklist; the mobile app build is the only route.
primary.how_to_play: Preserve the Android or iOS app build on compatible hardware/emulation where legally available; document delisting/store availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: Likely delisted; treat as preservation entry, not a current storefront recommendation.

entries.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Blacklist
entries.definitive_edition: Windows Deluxe/current release with Homeland DLC

primary.version: Deluxe/current PC release with Homeland DLC
primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity route and supports the main campaign, co-op missions, Spies vs. Mercs, and DLC/map content when installed; Wii U has unique GamePad controls but lacks co-op.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Deluxe/current release with Homeland DLC and bonus maps installed; document server status for online modes.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster; document DLC entitlements and server status for co-op/Spies vs. Mercs.
